children.text: apare māheśvarāḥ parameśvaratādātmyavādino'pi piṇḍasthairye sarvābhimatā jīvanmuktiḥ setsyatītyāsthāya piṇḍasthairyopāyaṃ pāradādipadavedanīyaṃ rasameva saṃgirante rasasya pāradatvaṃ saṃsāraparapāraprāpaṇahetutvena ||
children.translated_text: Other <s>Māheśvaras</s>, although they teach identity with the supreme Lord, maintain that the liberation while living accepted by all will be established when the body is stable; therefore they proclaim that <s>rasa</s>, known through the technical terms beginning with mercury, is the means to bodily stability. <s>Rasa</s> is mercury because it is the cause of reaching the far shore beyond saṃsāra.
That has been said:

children.text: saṃsārasya paraṃ pāraṃ datte'sau pāradaḥ smṛta iti ||
children.translated_text: "Since it gives the farthest shore of saṃsāra, it is remembered as <s>pārada</s>."
And also in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>:
"Mercury was declared by the best adepts for the sake of others,
O goddess, this sleeping one, equal to me, has arisen from my very limbs.
Because it is the fluid essence of my body, therefore it is called <s>rasa</s>."
Thus.

children.text: prakārāntareṇāpi jīvanmuktiyuktau neyaṃ vācoyuktiryuktimatīti cen na ṣaṭsvapi darśaneṣu dehapātānantaraṃ mukter uktatayā tatra viśvāsānupapattyā nirvicikitsapravṛtteranupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is objected, "Even if liberation while living is explained in another way, this verbal argument is not reasonable," that is not so; for in all six systems liberation is taught only after the fall of the body, and because confidence in that is impossible, decisive engagement without doubt is impossible.
That too has been stated in the same way:
"Even in the six systems liberation is shown at the falling of the body;
although it is said to be as clear as an āmalaka fruit in the hand, it is not directly perceived.
Therefore one should preserve that body by means of rasas and rasāyanas."
And by <s>Govindabhagavatpādācārya</s> also:
"Thus, considering wealth, body, and enjoyments to be permanent, one should always make effort;

children.text: muktau sā ca jñānāt taccābhyāsāt sa ca sthire dehe iti ||
children.translated_text: for liberation depends on knowledge, that on practice, and that on a stable body."

children.text: nanu vinaśvaratayā dṛśyamānasya dehasya kathaṃ nityatvam avamīyata iti cenmaivaṃ maṃsthāḥ ṣāṭkauśikasya śarīrasyānityatve rasābhrakapadābhilapyaharagaurīsṛṣṭijātasya nityatvopapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is asked, "How can permanence be understood in regard to the body, which is seen to be perishable?" do not think so; although the body made of the six sheaths is impermanent, permanence is possible for the body produced from the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>, denoted by the technical terms <s>rasa</s> and mica.
So too in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>:
"Those who, without abandoning the body, have attained another birth from the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>,
those <s>rasa</s>-adepts are venerable; the host of mantras is their servant."

children.text: tasmājjīvanmuktiṃ samīhamānena yoginā prathamaṃ divyatanurvidheyā haragaurīsṛṣṭisaṃyogajanitatvaṃ ca rasasya harajatvenābhrakasya gaurīsambhavatvena tattadātmakatvamuktam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore a yogin who desires liberation while living must first produce a divine body. The identity of <s>rasa</s> and mica with those two is stated, since <s>rasa</s> is born from <s>Hara</s> and mica from <s>Gaurī</s>.

children.text: abhrakastava bījaṃ tu mama bījaṃ tu pāradaḥ
children.translated_text: "Mica is your seed, while mercury is my seed;
O goddess, the union of these two destroys death and poverty."

children.text: atyalpam idam ucyate devadaityamunimānavādiṣu bahavo rasasāmarthyād divyaṃ dehamāśritya jīvanmuktimāśritāḥ śrūyante raseśvarasiddhānte ||
children.translated_text: This is said only briefly. In the Raseśvara doctrine it is heard that many among gods, demons, sages, humans, and others, through the power of <s>rasa</s>, assumed a divine body and attained liberation while living.
"Some gods, beginning with <s>Maheśa</s>, demons headed by <s>Kāvya</s>,
sages beginning with the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, and kings beginning with <s>Someśvara</s>,
<s>Govindabhagavatpādācārya</s>, <s>Govindanāyaka</s>,
<s>Carvaṭi</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Vyāli</s>, <s>Kāpāli</s>, and <s>Kandalāyana</s>,
these and many other perfected ones indeed wander about liberated while living,
having obtained a body made of <s>rasa</s>, eloquent in accounts of identity with it."
Thus.
This very meaning was expounded by the supreme Lord to the supreme Goddess:
"O queen of the gods, bodily maintenance is obtained by the yoga of action.
The yoga of action is remembered as twofold: <s>rasa</s> and breath.

children.text: mūrchito harati vyādhīn mṛto jīvayati svayam
children.translated_text: When stupefied it removes diseases; when killed it itself gives life.
When bound, <s>rasa</s>, and also air, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, produces the state of moving in the sky."
The nature of the stupefied state too has been stated:
"When quicksilver becomes of many colors, abandoning dense instability,

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ dṛśyate yasya mūrchitaṃ taṃ vadanti hi ||
children.translated_text: and its characteristic is seen, they call it stupefied."

children.text: ārdratvaṃ ca ghanatvaṃ ca tejo gauravacāpalam
children.translated_text: "Moistness, density, brilliance, heaviness, and instability:

children.text: yasyaitāni na dṛśyante taṃ vidyān mṛtasūtakam
children.translated_text: when these are not seen in it, one should know that quicksilver as killed."
Thus.
Elsewhere the nature of the bound state also has been declared:
"Uninjured, lightly melting, brilliant, clear, and heavy,
with bursting when repeatedly heated: this is the mark of bound quicksilver."
Thus.

children.text: nanu haragaurīsṛṣṭisiddhau piṇḍasthairyamāsthātuṃ pāryate tatsiddhireva kathamiti cen na aṣṭādaśasaṃskāravaśāttadupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: If it is asked, "Granted that stability of the body may be assumed if the creation of <s>Hara</s> and <s>Gaurī</s> is established, but how is that itself established?" that is not so, because it is possible through the eighteen saṃskāras.
The teachers have said this:

children.text: tasya hi sādhanavidhau sudhiyāṃ pratikarmanirmalāḥ prathamam
children.translated_text: "In the procedure for preparing it, first, by the wise, purified at each operation,
the eighteen saṃskāras must be carefully known."
And those saṃskāras have been enumerated:
"Sweating, rubbing, stupefying, fixing, subliming, restraining, and regulating,
then kindling, swallowing mica, measuring, digesting, and covering,
internal liquefaction, external liquefaction, alkalizing, coloring, and projecting,
penetration and ingestion: thus alchemical operation is eighteenfold."

The detailed exposition of that has been set forth by ancient teachers such as <s>Govindabhagavatpādācārya</s>, the omniscient <s>Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭāraka</s>, and others; it is omitted here from fear of making the book too extensive.

children.text: na ca rasaśāstraṃ dhātuvādārthameveti mantavyaṃ dehavedhadvārā muktereva paramaprayojanatvāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor should it be thought that the science of <s>rasa</s> is only for transmutation of metals, since liberation itself, through penetration of the body, is its supreme purpose.
This is said in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>:
"O god, the penetration of metals which was granted by you, O supreme Lord,

children.text: taṃ dehavedham ācakṣva yena syāt khecarī gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: explain that as penetration of the body, by which the sky-moving state may arise.

children.text: yathā lohe tathā dehe kartavyaḥ sūtakaḥ satā
children.translated_text: As with metal, so with the body, good people should apply quicksilver.
O goddess, it produces the same conviction in body and metal:
first one should test it on metal; afterward one should apply it to the body."

children.text: nanu saccidānandātmakaparatattvasphuraṇādeva muktisiddhau kim anena divyadehasampādanaprayāseneti cet tad etad avārttaṃ vārttaśarīrālābhe tadvārttāyā ayogāt ||
children.translated_text: If someone says, "Since liberation is established simply from the shining forth of the supreme reality whose nature is being, consciousness, and bliss, what is the point of this effort to produce a divine body?" that is no objection, because without obtaining the body concerned, the matter concerning it is impossible.
This is said in the <s>Rasahṛdaya</s>:
"Consciousness and bliss, free from abundant constructs and intended through every path,
even if it has shone forth, what does it do for the class of creatures whose body has not shone forth?"
"A body made decrepit by old age and made painfully manifest by cough, asthma, and the like,
is not fit for samādhi, its range of intellect and senses being obstructed.
A child of sixteen years is greedy for the taste of sense-objects; afterward,
as an old mortal whose discrimination has gone, how could he attain liberation?"

children.text: nanu jīvatvaṃ nāma saṃsāritvaṃ tadviparītatvaṃ muktatvaṃ tathā ca parasparaviruddhayoḥ katham ekāyatanatvam upapannaṃ syāditi cet tad anupapannaṃ vikalpānupapatteḥ muktistāvat sarvatīrthakarasaṃmatā sā kiṃ jñeyapade niviśate na vā carame śaśaviṣāṇakalpā syāt prathame na jīvanaṃ varjanīyamajīvato jñātṛtvānupapatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: If someone says, "Being a living soul means being subject to saṃsāra, and being liberated is the opposite of that; therefore how could two mutually opposed states have one and the same locus?" that is not tenable, because the alternative cannot be made out. Liberation, first of all, is accepted by all founders of systems. Does it fall within the object to be known or not? In the latter case it would be like a hare's horn; in the former, living cannot be excluded, since one who is not alive cannot be a knower.
This is said in the <s>Raseśvarasiddhānta</s>:
"O low-minded one, liberation while living, taught on the immeasurable path marked by <s>rasa</s> (mercury), does exist
among the other doctrines that depend on distinctions of reasoning.
Know that this knowable thing is to be known by knowledge; it is approved in all mantras.
One who is not alive will not know the knowable; therefore living certainly exists."

children.text: na cedamadṛṣṭacaramiti mantavyaṃ viṣṇusvāmimatānusāribhiḥ nṛpañcāsyaśarīrasya nityatvopapādanāt ||
children.translated_text: Nor should this be considered something never seen before, since the followers of <s>Viṣṇusvāmin</s>'s doctrine establish the eternality of the man-lion's body.
This is said in the <s>Sākārasiddhi</s>:
"I revere him, whose single form is being, consciousness, eternal, innate, inconceivable, complete bliss,
the man-lion, accepted by glorious <s>Viṣṇusvāmin</s>."

children.text: nanvetat sāvayavaṃ rūpavad avabhāsamānaṃ nṛkaṇṭhoravāṅgaṃ saditi na saṃgacchata ityādinākṣepapuraḥsaraṃ sanakādipratyakṣaṃ sahasraśīrṣā puruṣa ityādiśruti tamadbhutaṃ bālakamambujekṣaṇaṃ caturbhujaṃ śaṅkhagadādyudāyudham ityādi purāṇalakṣaṇena pramāṇatrayeṇa siddhaṃ nṛpañcānanāṅgaṃ kathamasat syāditi ||
children.translated_text: If the objection is first raised, "This visible form, possessing parts, with human neck, chest, and limbs, cannot properly be real," and so on, how could the body of the man-lion be unreal when it is established by the threefold proof: the direct perception of <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, the Śruti passage "the thousand-headed Person," and the Purāṇic mark such as "that wondrous boy, lotus-eyed, four-armed, holding up the conch, mace, and other weapons"?
The qualifiers beginning with "real" have been explained by <s>Garbhaśrīkāntamiśra</s>, whose inner being was devoted to the feet of <s>Viṣṇusvāmin</s>.

children.text: tasmād adiṣṭadehanityatvam atyantādṛṣṭaṃ na bhavatīti puruṣārthakāmukaiḥ puruṣaireṣṭavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the eternality of a desired body is not something utterly unseen, and it should be sought by people who desire the aims of human life.
For just this reason it is said:
"What supreme good is there other than the undecaying and immortal body alone, the abode of the sciences
and the root of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation?"
And <s>rasendra</s> (mercury) alone is capable of making one undecaying and immortal. Thus it says:
"That one king <s>rasa</s> makes the body undecaying and immortal."

children.text: kiṃ varṇyate rasasya māhātmyaṃ darśanasparśanādināpi mahatphalaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Why describe the greatness of <s>rasa</s>? Even by seeing, touching, and so on, there is a great result.
This is said in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>:
"From seeing it, touching it, eating it, and even remembering it,
and from worship of <s>rasa</s> and the gift of <s>rasa</s>, a sixfold result is seen.
Whatever liṅgas such as <s>Kedāra</s> exist on earth,

children.text: tāni dṛṣṭvā tu yatpuṇyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ rasadarśanādityādinā ||
children.translated_text: the merit gained by seeing them is that merit gained from seeing <s>rasa</s>," and so on.
Elsewhere too:
"Worship of the <s>rasa-liṅga</s> is more auspicious than all liṅgas such as those in <s>Kāśī</s>;
by it that liṅga is obtained, together with enjoyment, health, nectar, and immortality."
The negative consequence of reviling <s>rasa</s> is also shown:
"If, through negligence, a wise man hears reviling of <s>rasa</s>, he should remember this:
he should at once and always abandon the reviler, who is filled with inauspiciousness by reviling."

children.text: tasmādasmaduktayā rītyā divyaṃ dehaṃ sampādya yogābhyāsavaśāt paratattve dṛṣṭe puruṣārthaprāptirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after producing a divine body in the manner stated by us, when the supreme reality is seen through the force of yogic practice, the human aim is attained.
Then:
"For some whose vision is meritorious, the consciousness-made light that is situated between the two eyebrows,
shining like fire, lightning, and the sun and illuminating the world, opens forth.
The supreme, whose single essence is highest bliss, whose nature is supreme light, free from conceptual division,
from which the impurities and afflictions have melted away, is to be known as peaceful and self-cognized.

children.text: tasminnādhāya manaḥ sphuradakhilaṃ cinmayaṃ jagat paśyan
children.translated_text: Placing the mind in that, seeing the whole shining world as consciousness-made,
with the bondage of karma destroyed, one attains Brahmanhood even here."
And Śruti says:

children.text: raso vai saḥ rasaṃ hyevāyaṃ labdhvānandībhavatīti ||
children.translated_text: "He indeed is <s>rasa</s>; for, having obtained <s>rasa</s>, this one becomes blissful."
Thus it is established that <s>rasa</s> alone is the means for crossing the heavy mass of other suffering.

children.text: tathāca rasasya parabrahmaṇā sāmyamiti pratipādakaḥ ślokaḥ
children.translated_text: And accordingly there is a verse that teaches the similarity of <s>rasa</s> with the supreme Brahman:

children.text: yaḥ syāt prāvaraṇāvimocanadhiyāṃ sādhyaḥ prakṛtyā punaḥ sampanno sahate na dīvyati paraṃ vaiśvānare jāgrati
children.translated_text: "That which is to be accomplished by those intent on removing coverings, and again is naturally perfected, endures and does not sport beyond when the universal fire is awake;

children.text: jāto yadyaparaṃ na vedayati ca svasmāt svayaṃ dyotate yo brahmaiva sa dainyasaṃsṛtibhayāt pāyādasau pārada iti ||
children.translated_text: if born, it makes nothing else known and shines by itself from itself: may that mercury, which is Brahman itself, protect us from the fear of wretched transmigration."
Thus ends the Raseśvara doctrine in the <s>Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha</s>.
